query: Which method can be used for the presence of ferromagnetic ground states, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Spin‐polarized density functional theory (DFT) analysis using the Stoner criterion will predict ferromagnetic ground states reliably because when the product of the density of states at the Fermi level (N(E_F)) and the Stoner exchange parameter (I) exceeds unity, the exchange interactions favor a spin‐split (ferromagnetic) state.
generation.material_initial_state: A material modeled in a non‐spin‐polarized DFT simulation representing a non-magnetic electronic configuration.
generation.intervention: Perform spin‐polarized DFT calculations to determine the density of states at the Fermi level and estimate the Stoner parameter. Compare the total energies of spin-polarized (magnetic) and non‐spin‐polarized (non-magnetic) states.
generation.conditions: Zero-temperature (0 K) or static lattice conditions using a selected exchange‐correlation functional, with no external magnetic field applied.
generation.structural_mediator: The intrinsic crystal and electronic structure that yields a high density of states at the Fermi level, which is critical for meeting the Stoner criterion.
generation.mechanism: If N(E_F) multiplied by the Stoner parameter I exceeds one, the gain in exchange energy from aligning spins will overcome the associated kinetic energy cost, leading the system to stabilize in a ferromagnetic (spin-split) ground state.
generation.predicted_outcome: Materials that satisfy the condition N(E_F)·I > 1 will exhibit a lower total energy in spin‐polarized DFT calculations compared to their non‐magnetic counterparts, accompanied by a finite calculated magnetic moment.
generation.baseline: Results from non‐spin‐polarized DFT calculations that predict a non-magnetic ground state.
generation.boundary: The predictive accuracy may be limited by the choice of exchange‐correlation functional, treatment of electron correlations, and neglect of thermal effects; thus, the method is most reliable for systems where DFT approximations hold well.
generation.uncertainty: The exact numerical threshold and the sensitivity of N(E_F) and I values may vary with system specifics and computational parameters, requiring experimental verification for confirmation.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a range of materials with varying computed values of N(E_F) and estimated Stoner parameters. For each material, conduct both non‐spin‐polarized and spin‐polarized DFT calculations to determine the total energy and magnetic moment. Analyze whether materials with N(E_F)·I > 1 consistently exhibit a lower energy in the spin‐polarized state.
measurements: Total energy of the spin‐polarized state versus the non‐spin‐polarized state
Calculated density of states at the Fermi level
Estimated Stoner parameter and computed product N(E_F)·I
Resultant magnetic moment per formula unit
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If any material with a computed value of N(E_F)·I > 1 does not show a statistically significant lower energy and a finite magnetic moment in the spin‐polarized state relative to the non‐magnetic state, then the hypothesis is falsified.
